paragraphs.text: Clue is a predefined token and artifact type . Clue tokens are colorless artifacts with " , Sacrifice this token: Draw a card ". The investigate keyword action creates a Clue token and does nothing else. Clues are usually created by investigating, but some cards create Clues directly, without investigate; this distinction only matters to the few cards which specifically care about the investigate keyword. Some artifact cards have the Clue subtype; these often function similarly to Clue tokens, but they don't inherently share the abilities of the predefined token.

Investigate and Clues were introduced in Shadows over Innistrad . This was the first major set mechanic involving an artifact token, and it paved the way for other tokens such as Treasure and Food . Avatar: The Last Airbender was the first set to feature Clue tokens as a major mechanic without using investigate.

Investigation is sometimes triggered by specific events, such as a land entering the battlefield ( Tireless Tracker ) or a creature dying ( Ulvenwald Mysteries ). Some cards also have abilities that trigger when a Clue is sacrificed (Lazav, Wearer of Faces), which adds strategic depth to the decision about when to use a Clue.

Clues can be easily compared to cantrips , in that if one immediately spends the mana to draw a card, the total cost is like other spells that draw a card. However, the capacity to "store" the card to draw later is a major appeal to the ability, as it improves the mana efficiency of the original spell. Breaking up the cost lets the player decide when the card is needed, saving it for after other spells are expended. That said, investigating becomes more and more unwieldy the more it's done, as one needs sufficient mana to sacrifice them all, exemplified by Confirm Suspicions : with enough mana, it's four cards for one; without enough mana, it's five mana to answer one card. As such, it's a way to demonstrate the relation between tempo and mana, like its use in Murders at Karlov Manor , where the format generally supplies Clues as artifacts to sacrifice, as opposed to Treasure or Food .

Clue tokens were designed for Shadows over Innistrad (2016) to capture the flavor of investigating a mystery. An earlier version of the investigate mechanic used impulsive draw , but this proved too powerful. A mini design team led by Dave Humpherys looked for a replacement. The team was inspired by cluestones from the set's worldbuilding, which led them to experiment with artifact tokens and settle on the final design. Several mana costs were experimented with; was chosen as a meaningful, but not insurmountable, cost.

The design of Clues opened up space for other artifact tokens, and predefined artifact tokens would eventually become a major design tool. Other examples include Treasure , Food , and Blood . Because Clues are the first of their kind, they don't follow all the design principles of later artifact tokens: their cost doesn't involve tapping , and their creation is tied to a named keyword (investigate). The name "investigate" persisted on later cards due to its resonant flavor .

Fae Offering and Academy Manufactor from Modern Horizons 2 (2021) were the first cards to create Clue tokens without investigating. Both cards group several predefined tokens by name, so creating Clues directly avoids an unnecessary split of the ability. As a consequence, Clue became a predefined token (the rules text of Clue tokens had previously been defined by the investigate keyword). This decision did not make investigate obsolete .

Investigate was reused on five cards in Innistrad: Midnight Hunt (2021) as a callback to Shadows over Innistrad . By 2022, investigate and Clue tokens had become deciduous . Investigate appeared again in Murders at Karlov Manor as a main set mechanic, where it was used in several ways (e.g. as a trigger or on spells ).

Avatar: The Last Airbender (2025) is the first set to have standalone Clue creation as a major set mechanic. This was done to better match the flavor of Clues in the set, which was more about villains tracking down the protagonists than solving a mystery. It also reduced the number of keywords in the set and brought Clues in line with other predefined tokens. They synergise well with both waterbending as an artifact to tap and firebending as a mid-combat activated ability. Investigate can still be used in other sets, if it is flavorfully appropriate; however, it has lost its deciduous status and now has a Storm Scale rating of 4. Investigate appeared again in Marvel Super Heroes (2026) as a cameo on two cards.

The first card printed with the Clue subtype was Parcel Myr from Modern Horizons 2 . Most typed Clues have the default Clue ability, with two deviations: Candy Trail (the first card printed with multiple predefined token subtypes ) requires a tap and gains three life as befitting its shared status as a food , while Found Footage surveils 2.
The Ravnica Cluestones ( 10 cards ) could have been Clues if this type had already existed.
